Venture.title: Venture
Venture.description: Represents a venture within the EveCount portfolio.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Venture entity.

sector.description: The sector the venture operates in (e.g., FinTech, Health).

status.description: The current status of the venture (e.g., Live).

Submission.title: Submission
Submission.description: Represents a general application or submission to EveCount, for ventures, incubator, careers, or partnerships.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Submission entity.

applicationType.description: The type of application being submitted.

visionPitch.description: The vision pitched by the potential partner, or a statement of interest.

companyName.description: Name of the company submitting the idea or inquiry.

submitterName.description: Name of the person who submitted the application.

contactPhone.description: Contact phone number of the submitter.

portfolioUrl.description: URL to a portfolio, LinkedIn, or GitHub profile.

resumeUrl.description: URL to a resume or CV.

roleInterest.description: The role or area of interest for a career application.

partnershipInterest.description: Details about the partnership or sponsorship interest.

message.description: A general message or cover letter, primarily for career inquiries.

ventureId.description: Reference to Venture, if the submission led to a venture. (Relationship: Venture 1:N Submission)

definition.description: Collection for storing venture data. Each document represents a single venture.
Collection for storing submissions from potential partners. Includes submission details such as vision pitch, submission date, submitter name, and contact email.

firestore.reasoning: The Firestore structure is designed to manage ventures and submissions within the EveCount platform, emphasizing security, scalability, and ease of maintenance. It prioritizes authorization independence by avoiding hierarchical authorization dependencies and denormalizing authorization contexts where necessary. The structure segregates data with different access needs into separate collections to simplify security rules and ensure that rules are not used as filters. Access is modeled using path-based ownership for user-related data and membership maps for collaborative data, following consistent patterns to enhance clarity and predictability. Submissions are stored in a single collection, even from anonymous users, to provide a streamlined approach to data capture. This design choice simplifies security rules by avoiding the need to differentiate between authenticated and anonymous submissions. This supports required QAPs by avoiding filtering data based on authentication state and instead, focusing on securing data at rest with appropriate security rules.
